1) Psychodynamic theory is the most influential theory in the psychology of personality, as it has been the most cited in the literature; 2) The psychodynamic theory of personality has been used in the study of a wide range of psychological phenomena, from personality traits, to the self, to the study of mental disorders, to the study and treatment of interpersonal relationships; 3) The psychodynamic approach has been used to investigate the development of personality, as well as its change and modification

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the psychodynamic perspective is a theoretical framework which, in the first instance, focuses on the affective sources of the psychological facts and, in the second instance, on the role of the affect in shaping (inter) subjectivity.
psychodynamic psychology is the psychology grounded on the assumption that the affective source shapes (inter)subjectivities.
psychodynamic theory is the theory of psychological processes and facts as they are shaped by their dynamic (affective) source.

The main takeaway from our work is that
psychodynamic theories are characterized by an unbearable tension between the necessity to explain and the impossibility to do so.
psychodynamic theory is not a monolithic theory, but a set of theories that share a common ground.

psychodynamically oriented theories are the theories which assume that psychological facts (inter)subjective and objective, conscious or unconscious, individual or collective) are shaped by conflicts, and that these conflicts are rooted in affective processes.
